summary: Sticky version handover latency during regional cutover causing graceful fallback and mixed responses
description:
Issue summary:
BrightForms reported multiple customer sessions receiving mixed model outputs during a scheduled regional cutover. Customer had explicitly pinned to redwood/open-7b-v2 for their tenant. During the cutover, some long-lived sessions transitioned to a fallback variant (redwood/open-7b-quant) despite the pin being present in the tenant config.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests for the tenant returned responses from the quantized variant for 18 minutes.
- Increased token latency for affected requests (~250ms p50 -> ~420ms p50) and small but visible quality regressions in returned completions.
- Customer reported degraded UX for chat widgets in production; potential SLA breach risk.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-east with cross-region standby in us-west.
- Tenant: brightforms-prod, pinned_version: redwood/open-7b-v2.
- Cutover window: regional DNS migration + routing rebalancer job at 2025-03-04T02:12:00Z.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Reproduce by creating a tenant with a long-lived streaming session pinned to open-7b-v2.
2) Trigger a simulated regional failover (reroute edge traffic from us-east to us-west replicas).
3) Observe session affinity & pin state while orchestrator performs snapshot merge and connectivity re-establishment.

Observed behavior:
- Orchestrator snapshot merge completed but edge session handles reconnected to a replica that had an older routing snapshot where the tenant pin was present but the local cache considered the pinned worker draining.
- Smart-routing applied a temporary fallback policy (favoring quantized variant in us-west to meet latency SLO) and injected fallback routing for inflight sessions before remote pin reconciliation finished.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant pin must be preserved across handover with deterministic session affinity; inflight sessions should either wait for pin reconciliation or be routed to the pinned variant without silent fallback.

Logs & traces (examples):
- Edge trace: https://grafana.redwood/trace/edge/trace-9a7c1 (shows reconnect at 2025-03-04T02:12:10Z)
- Orchestrator snapshot merge: https://concourse.redwood/builds/merge-5249 (status: success)
- Serving runtime logs (worker-us-west-3): tail /var/log/worker-1234.log includes "pin-check: missing-active-worker -> triggering-fallback" entries.

Workaround used by Support:
- Forced a soft rebind: triggered tenant pin refresh from control plane (admin API call: POST /admin/tenants/brightforms-prod/force-pin-refresh) which initiated immediate reconciliation and cleared fallbacks after ~6 minutes.
comments: Maya Patel (2025-03-04 03:05 UTC): Customer contacted Support — attached session IDs and sample request/response pairs showing differing completions. Customer says this occurred after our scheduled regional cutover.
Ethan Ross (2025-03-04 03:20 UTC): Acknowledged. Raising to P1. Collecting traces from edge, orchestrator, and worker logs. Opening investigation channel #support and paging oncall-sre.

Oncall-SRE (R. Chen) (2025-03-04 03:27 UTC): Early signal shows snapshot-merge completed but there was a short window where edge accepted reconnects before control plane propagated pin commits to the worker cache. Correlating with rebalancer logs.

SRE (2025-03-04 03:40 UTC): Forced pin refresh via admin API as a mitigation — observed fallthrough drop from ~12% to <1% within 6 minutes. Noted that affected sessions were primarily long-lived streaming websocket connections.

Maya Patel (2025-03-04 04:12 UTC): Customer confirmed improved behavior after mitigation. They've requested root cause analysis and log evidence for their audit team. Also asked for plan to prevent recurrence during future cutovers.
Ethan Ross (2025-03-05 09:18 UTC): Investigation continues. Adding related PRs for a proposed fix to snapshot reconciliation ordering. Will attach postmortem once RCA complete.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge reconnect ordering allowed session attach to worker before worker applied latest pin snapshot — resulting in routing decision to fallback variant based on local draining signals.
Hypothesis 2: Smart-routing fallback heuristics are too eager when local worker reports reduced capacity during cross-region rebind; it doesn't consult pinned-version authoritative flag atomically.

Evidence: Worker logs show 'pin-snapshot-applied' at 2025-03-04T02:18:02Z but edge reconnects routed traffic starting at 2025-03-04T02:12:10Z. Control plane commit time 02:11:59Z; propagation to worker cache delayed by ~6 minutes due to snapshot merge order and backoff retries.
Dashboards: Per-tenant routing breakdown dashboard shows spike in fallback routing percentage correlated with DNS TTL expiry and rebalancer job time window.

Reproducer notes: Using a heavy streaming session and toggling rebalancer triggers the window reliably. Shorter sessions (<= 30s) rarely affected due to normal session termination and new connection establishing post-reconciliation.

Edge case: If a worker reports 'draining' flag because of scheduled maintenance, smart-routing currently prefers latency-preserving fallback even when a tenant pin exists — logic is by design to protect SLOs but needs stricter pin precedence.
Potential customer impact severity: High — quality regression and potential data residency concerns if fallbacks cross region/model constraints.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: Admin pin-refresh forced reconciliation which restored correct routing for inflight sessions within ~6 minutes.

Short term fix planned: Adjust smart-routing to treat a validated tenant pin as an authoritative override when deciding fallback choices during snapshot gaps. Add backoff jitter to edge reconnect path to reduce out-of-order attachment during cutovers.

Long term fix: Change snapshot apply sequence so control plane publishes 'pin-ready' marker and workers block accepting session attaches for pinned tenants until marker observed. Add unit/integration tests covering streaming session rebind across snapshot merges.
Customer communication: Sent interim incident summary and mitigation steps to BrightForms on 2025-03-05. Committed to a technical RCA and timeline for fixes by 2025-03-12.
Follow-ups: Create INT task to update runbook for regional cutovers and include a pre-cutover pin-state validation step (INT-731210). Schedule engineering RFC for snapshot reconciliation change.
